title: CSP nonce is a hardcoded constant and no script carries it
evidence: The nonce 'r4nd0m' is a literal in a static HTML file, so it is the same for every response and is visible in the source. None of the three script tags on the page (about.html:8-10) has a nonce attribute.
failing_case: An attacker who can inject markup into this page adds <script nonce="r4nd0m">...</script> and the CSP allows it, because the nonce is public and never changes. A nonce protects only if it is fresh per response. The legitimate scripts get no benefit from it, since none has the attribute.
remediation: Drop the nonce from the static file. Either generate it per response on the server and set it on both the header and the tags, or use 'sha384-...' hash sources for the inline and third-party scripts.

title: lib.js from cdn.example.org is blocked by script-src 'self' 'nonce-...' (host not allowed, tag has no nonce)
evidence: Driven in Chromium: Refused to load the script 'https://cdn.example.org/lib.js' ... script-src 'self' 'nonce-r4nd0m'. Only an allowed host, a matching nonce or a hash source would let it load; integrity= alone does not.
failing_case: Visitor opens /about: lib.js never runs, so any page code that depends on it fails.
remediation: Give the tag a per-response nonce, or remove it, or allow the named host. Pick one policy and apply it in the meta tag and _headers.

title: The map iframe is blocked by the page's own CSP (no frame-src, falls back to default-src 'self')
evidence: Driven in Chromium: "Refused to frame 'https://www.example.org/' because it violates ... default-src 'self'. Note that frame-src was not explicitly set".
failing_case: A visitor opens /about and sees an empty box (with a console error) where the map should be. No fallback text or link is shown.
remediation: Add frame-src with the one map host to the CSP in the meta tag and in _headers, and put a plain link to the map inside the page as a fallback.

title: Analytics script on the checkout page is blocked by the CSP header from _headers
evidence: checkout.html has no meta CSP; the header in _headers line 2 (script-src 'self') applies to https://shop.example.com/*. Driven by serving that header locally: Refused to load the script 'https://stats.example.org/t.js'.
failing_case: A shopper completes checkout; the tracking script never loads, so the funnel drops its checkout events while the markup suggests it works.
remediation: Either allow that one host in the _headers script-src or remove the tag; do not run third-party scripts on the page that takes card numbers unless that is a deliberate decision.

title: Pay button on a checkout page with no total, no items and no busy state
evidence: checkout.html holds one card field and a 'Pay' button. No amount, order summary, currency or consent text appears, and nothing disables the button on submit.
failing_case: The user cannot see what they are charged. A double-click sends two POSTs to /pay, because the button is never disabled; with no idempotency key the card can be charged twice.
remediation: Show the order lines and total next to the button, label it 'Pay $X.XX', disable it on first submit and send an idempotency key with the request.

title: No viewport meta tag on any of the three pages
evidence: login.html, about.html and checkout.html have only charset, title, canonical and script tags in the head. None has <meta name="viewport">.
failing_case: On a 390 px phone the browser lays the page out at about 980 px and scales it down, so the sign-in and card fields render tiny and the user must pinch-zoom to type a card number. This fails reflow at 390 px.
remediation: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to every page, from a shared template.

title: The page's own CSP (script-src 'self') blocks the third-party widget script it loads
evidence: Served site/ locally and loaded login.html in Chromium (driven, third-party hosts stubbed). Console: Refused to load the script 'https://cdn.example.org/widget.js' because it violates ... "script-src 'self'". _headers (line 2) sets the same policy for https://shop.example.com/*, so the header blocks it too.
failing_case: Any visitor opening /login: the browser refuses cdn.example.org/widget.js, so whatever the widget does never runs, and the console shows a CSP error. The integrity and crossorigin attributes are wasted.
remediation: Decide whether the widget is needed. If so, add that one named host to script-src in both the meta tag and _headers (no wildcard); if not, remove the tag.

title: The same placeholder SRI hash is used on three different scripts
evidence: The value after sha384- is base64 for the text 'foobarbaz' repeated five times followed by 'qux', not a digest of any file. The identical string appears on cdn.example.org/widget.js (login.html:8), cdn.example.org/lib.js (about.html:8) and stats.example.org/t.js (checkout.html:7). Three different files cannot share one hash.
failing_case: The browser downloads each file, computes its SHA-384, finds it differs from the declared value and refuses to run the script. The widget, the library and the stats script all fail, and the integrity attribute gives only the look of protection.
remediation: Compute the real hash for each pinned file version (openssl dgst -sha384 -binary file | openssl base64 -A) and generate the attribute in the build. Fail the build when it does not match.

title: Sign-in fields have no autocomplete tokens
evidence: login.html:16-17 and about.html:18 collect the user's email and password with no autocomplete attribute. WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.5 (AA) asks for the purpose of fields about the user to be programmatically determinable.
failing_case: A password manager or browser autofill cannot reliably tell the email field is a username or the other is the current password, so users with motor or memory difficulties must retype credentials. This fails 1.3.5.
remediation: Add autocomplete="username" (or "email") and autocomplete="current-password" on login.html, and autocomplete="email" on the subscribe field.

title: A dev live-reload script over plain http from localhost is left in the shipped page
evidence: No integrity, no crossorigin, scheme is http on an https site (mixed content). Chromium currently refuses it only because the meta CSP lacks that host (driven, console error).
failing_case: A visitor who happens to run any local service on port 8080 (a dev server, a proxy, a malicious app) gets that service's JavaScript executed in the about page's origin as soon as the CSP is loosened or removed, for example when someone adds localhost to fix the console error. Today it also logs a CSP violation on every load.
remediation: Delete the tag from the committed file and inject reload scripts only in the dev server; add a CI check that rejects http:// and localhost script sources.

title: Link text shows shop.example.com but goes to www.example.com
evidence: The visible text names host shop.example.com, the page's own canonical host (about.html:6). The href goes to https://www.example.com/, a different host.
failing_case: A user reads 'Our shop lives at shop.example.com', clicks, and lands on www.example.com. If www is not the shop, the user is sent to a host the text does not name. This is the same pattern a phishing link uses, and anyone who controls that host gets traffic labelled as the shop.
remediation: Make the text and the href the same host: link to https://shop.example.com/ or change the text to match the real target.

title: Link text 'index.html' points at another site's root
evidence: The text looks like a file name on the page's own site. The target is https://docs.example.net/, a separate host with no file path. The adjacent link 'brochure.pdf' does match its target.
failing_case: A user expecting a local index.html page is taken off-site to docs.example.net. The link text names a file that does not exist at the target.
remediation: Use text that says where it goes, for example 'Documentation (docs.example.net)'.
